newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks end lower in afternoon selldown.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks end lower in afternoon selldown.

text.p: A selldown in the second half of the session took Malaysian stocks sharply lower across-the-board, dealers said.

Share prices were hit by a combination of profit-taking, forced selling related to settlement and uncertainty about Wall Street's direction, they said. "People are feeling a little bit jittery," said an institutional dealer.

The Composite Index finished above its session low of 1,257.88, down 10.23 points or 0.81 percent to 1,260.44. The Second Board slipped 5.04 points to 644.49. Shares started the day firmer but lost steam by midday.

Stock deliveries related to the seven-day settlement period also contributed to the market's decline, dealers said. In addition, some players may have been nervous about news that a shorter settlement of five days would be implemented by the third quarter, they said.
"To the extent this market is reliant on people who don't have money, even if you tighten it (settlement) by one day, it's impacting people's investment horizons," said a dealer.
William Chan, an institutional dealer at Seagroatt & Campbell, said, "If Wall Street goes up tonight, things will stabilise." The Dow lost 47 points on Friday.
